review_comment: User-provided input from HTTP request parameters flows directly into email template rendering without validation. The vulnerability occurs at line 79 where request.args values are assigned to substitutions dictionary. This allows potential injection of malicious content into email subjects and bodies. Implement input validation on all user-provided parameters before adding them to the substitutions dictionary.

User-provided data from HTTP requests is URL-encoded and embedded in email templates. The basic urllib.quote() encoding does not provide sufficient protection against injection attacks. Add input validation and sanitization before URL encoding to prevent malicious content from being injected into URLs within email templates.

User-provided data flows into email templates without comprehensive sanitization. Only specific fields are HTML-escaped, while others remain vulnerable to XSS if templates are not secured. The patch adds partial protection but does not address all injection points. Ensure all user inputs used in email templates are sanitized before rendering.
